findings.title: --flusher-processes defaults to 1, so the PR's per-shard process model is not the default
findings.body: The new `--flusher-processes` option defaults to 1. The factory passes this to `SpanFlusher(max_processes=...)`, so with the default every assigned shard is handled by a single flusher process. The PR description says the flusher should spawn a process per redis shard, and the flusher docstring says the same. Production consumers that don't set the flag keep the old single-process throughput, which is the bottleneck this change is meant to remove. The help text 'Defaults to 1' also contradicts the 'one process per shard' behaviour. Either the default should be unset/None (meaning one process per shard) or the description and rollout plan should say the scaling is opt-in.

findings.title: New flusher_processes parameter inserted before produce_to_pipe shifts positional arguments
findings.body: `flusher_processes` was added between `output_block_size` and `produce_to_pipe`. Any existing caller that passes `produce_to_pipe` positionally will now pass it into `flusher_processes`, silently breaking the call. The new parameter should be appended after `produce_to_pipe` or made keyword-only.

findings.title: _create_process_for_shard is dead code and would restart the wrong thing if used
findings.body: `_create_process_for_shard` (singular) is never called; `_ensure_processes_alive` restarts by process index. The method also restarts the whole process that owns the shard, which kills the other shards' flushing in that process without going through the kill/restart bookkeeping (`process_restarts`). It should be removed or wired up correctly.

findings.title: Memory info is summed across per-process buffers, which may double-count Redis usage
findings.body: `submit` now collects `get_memory_info()` from every per-process `SpansBuffer` and sums `used` and `available`. Shards that map to the same redis node (or each buffer reporting the cluster-wide figure) will be counted multiple times, skewing the used/available ratio. The hard-backpressure threshold `spans.buffer.max-memory-percentage` then trips at the wrong level. Memory info should be de-duplicated per redis node or taken from a single buffer.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag keys: 'shard' vs 'shards'
findings.body: The produce timer and segment size metrics use the tag `shard`, but the wait_produce timer uses `shards`. Dashboards and alerts filtering on `shard` will miss the wait_produce data, and the same dimension is split across two keys. Use one key consistently.

findings.title: test_basic relies on sleep to wait for a background thread/process
findings.body: The test adds `time.sleep(0.1)` with the comment 'Give flusher threads time to process', then calls `join()`. This is timing-dependent and will be flaky on slow CI, and the test also changes from `django_db` to `transaction=True` without explanation. Synchronize on the flush result (e.g. poll until messages appear with a deadline) instead of a fixed sleep.

findings.title: test_flusher_processes_limit only checks structure, not that flushing works across processes
findings.body: The new test asserts the number of processes and shard distribution, but never submits spans or checks that segments from shards handled by the shared process get flushed. The multi-shard-per-process path, which is the new behaviour, is untested for correctness, and restart behaviour is not covered either.

findings.title: Added 'hasattr vs isinstance' guidance is unrelated to this PR and misleading
findings.body: The new 'WRONG: Use hasattr() for unions' example uses `x = 'hello'` with a `str | None` annotation and calls `hasattr(x, 'replace')`. This is not a real union-narrowing bug, and the rule as stated overgeneralises: hasattr is a legitimate duck-typing check. The change also has nothing to do with the span flusher. It should be dropped from this PR or rewritten to describe an actual problem.
